title: Adaptive Dedicated Packaging & SLA Tiering Playbook
creator: Sophie Chen
description: Create an operational playbook and go-to-market packaging for Dedicated GPU capacity that supports adaptive reservation bands, explicit SLA tiers, and controlled burst capacity. The playbook will define product SKUs, pricing levers, contract language for enterprise SAs, and the rollout plan with Sales and Solutions Engineering. It must balance predictable revenue (commits) with customer needs for headroom, while preserving capacity isolation and clear billing semantics.
acceptance_criteria: Package definitions: three SLA tiers (Bronze/Silver/Gold) with clear throughput/latency targets and failure allowances
Pricing model: committed monthly SKU + burst credits pricing table with worked examples for small/medium/large customers
Contract language: draft SOW/SQ clauses for reserved capacity, burst behavior, failure/fallback guarantees, and change control
Internal playbook: Sales play, SE collateral, cost calculator spreadsheet, and a rollout checklist
Operational hooks: mapping from SLA tier to autoscaling policy, monitoring alerts, and runbook for degraded capacity
Sign-off from Revenue, Legal, Security, and Runtime Engineering on definitions and risk mitigations
updates: 2025-02-16 - Kickoff with Sales, Revenue Ops, and Runtime Eng. Aligned on goal: reduce friction for enterprise procurement while enabling predictable capacity economics.
2025-02-21 - Defined preliminary SLA tiers (throughput bands + p95/p99 latency targets). Runtime Eng requested additional telemetry to enforce SLOs; added ENG-1842 as dependency.

2025-02-28 - Pricing workshop with Finance. Agreed to anchor commit pricing to $/GPU-hour equivalents and to offer burst credits at a premium rate rather than percentage overage. Finance requested margin floor checks for 3 customer archetypes.

2025-03-03 - Legal provided initial contract language notes: require explicit definition of 'burst', cap on sustained burst sequences, and change-control for capacity scale-down. Marked security_review_required.
2025-03-05 - Draft playbook circulated to Revenue and Solutions Engineering for feedback. Collected SE notes about common ask: flexible region pinning and predictable failover to hosted variants.
2025-03-05 - Action: build cost calculator and three customer example pages (SMB, Mid-market, Enterprise) before next review on 2025-03-12.
decisions: Use fixed commit SKUs (monthly) by strata: Small (2-8 GPUs), Mid (9-64 GPUs), Large (65+ GPUs) to simplify quoting for Sales
Implement a 'burst credits' token model that consumes credits at a 2x rate vs committed usage and caps at a configurable daily limit per contract

Expose three SLA tiers: Bronze (best-effort with 99.5% windowed availability), Silver (SLA with response-time objectives + priority support), Gold (financial SLA, 99.95% availability + 4hr incident SLA)
Autoscaling tie-ins: Gold customers get pre-configured autoscale headroom and reserved burst lanes; Bronze customers can burst into shared pool with no guaranteed throughput

Billing semantics: committed usage billed monthly at discounted rate; burst credits invoiced monthly as consumed with a separate line item; overage fallback to hosted compatible model priced at a premium as last-resort
tradeoffs: Simplicity vs accuracy: coarse commit SKUs reduce quoting complexity but may misprice highly spiky customers
Capacity isolation vs utilization: strict isolation improves reliability but reduces overall platform utilization and increases cost
Contract flexibility vs operational predictability: shorter commit terms (monthly) increase customer adoption but make capacity forecasting harder
Pricing transparency vs competitive differentiation: published burst pricing simplifies procurement but may be gamed by customers to avoid commits
risks: Underpricing burst-heavy customers could lead to sustained losses if customers routinely use burst > daily cap
Legal pushback on financial SLA wording could delay enterprise contracts
Runtime telemetry gaps (ENG-1842) may prevent reliable enforcement of per-contract burst caps
Complex quoting workflow could increase SE time per deal if the cost calculator is not embedded in Salesforce
next_steps: Complete cost calculator with 3 archetypes and validate with Finance by 2025-03-10
Implement telemetry changes in ENG-1842 to capture per-contract burst consumption and enforce caps
Iterate contract language with Legal; prepare redlineable SQ template and SOW clauses by 2025-03-20
Create Sales/SE enablement: one-pager, demo scripts, and sample quotes for Q2 pilots
Run internal pilot with 2 existing customers (Ops-approval) to validate billing flow and autoscale behavior before public launch
